sentences.text:
M/S. Vidya Nagar Plot Owners ... vs The Principal Secretary on 2
September, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Writ Petition No.20762 of 2020
Order :

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking the following relief:
"....to pass an Order or Direction more particularly in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the inaction of the Respondents in not disposing the Representation dated 28/09/2020 addressed by the petitioner society with regard to the unauthorized acquisition of its members residential plots covered by registered Sale Deeds from the unofficial respondents who are in hand in glow conspired colluded with the official Respondents 4 and 5 resulting illegal allotment of the residential plots by virtue of 3rd Respondent Proceedings No.E/1699/2017, dated 17/02/2018 without following due process of law without causing notice and without paying compensation is illegal arbitrary and unconstitutional consequently direct the Respondents 2 to 5 to dispose the Petitioners Representation dated 28/9/2020 expeditiously in the interest of justice and to grant...."

2. The brief facts of the case are that respondent Nos.6 to 13 purchased 19 Acres of land under two separate sale deeds in Sy.No.133, situated at Appaipally village, Wanaparthy Mandal and District,
which are developed into residential plots each admeasuring 100 to 150 sq.yards under layout in the year 2006.

The said persons in collusion and conspiracy with office of Tahsildar officials, Sub- registrar officials Wanaparthy played a fraud, manipulation of records and sold the total residential plots under monthly payment scheme w.e.f., 2006 to the innocent and bonafide purchasers in the open market.
Most of the purchasers belong to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes.

In the year 2018 when the government came with a sign board in the residential sight, following announcement by the Collector, Wanaparthy and local MLA with regard to the construction of Government Hospital in the land to an extent of Acs.8.00 guntas in Sy.No.133, situated at Appaipally village,
Wanaparthy, which is totally covering the hundreds of residential plots of the petitioners.

Shocked by the incident, the bonafide purchasers who have been in possession of the residential plots since 2006 after knowing the alleged government claim has made enquiry and came to the fact that respondent Nos.6 to 13 cheated them by manipulating the revenue records and suppression of government claim by the SRO, Wanaparthy.
The revenue records will not match with the government alleged claim.
The self contrary and irrelevant statements and irregular Revenue records clearly establishes a fact that they played a fraud, cheating and duped the innocent purchasers.
Hence, the present writ petition.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner - Society would submit that the petitioner - Society addressed the representation dated 28.09.2020 to respondent Nos.1 to 5, though the registered post M/S. Vidya Nagar Plot Owners ... vs The Principal Secretary on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41610970/
1 stating that the members of the petitioner - Society demonstrated the conspiracy and fraud played by respondent Nos.6 to 13 in collusion and hand in glow with respondent Nos.4 and 5, who allowed the registration of the residential plots in schemes and sold the same to approximately 200 members.
Despite receiving the said representation, the respondent authorities did not act upon the same.
Aggrieved by the said inaction, the petitioner filed the present writ petition.

4. Opposing the same, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, for respondent Nos.3 to 5 would submit that the land in Sy.No.133 of Appaipally village of Wanaparthy Mandal and District is government land and it was assigned to ST beneficiaries under a condition of not to alienate/transfer to any one as per POT Act, 1977, the said assigned lands are not transferable/alienable and such alienations are not valid in the eyes of law.
In the said assign land the private persons made a layout including other private lands nearby and sold away the said plots to the public.
Soon after noticing the same transactions the Tahsildar resumed the land in favour of the Government by following due procedure issuing notices.

5. Learned Assistant Government Pleader further submitted that as per the requisition of the Medical and Health Department Wanaparthy, the earlier resumed land was alloted for construction of District Hospital vide District Collector proceedings No.E/1699/2017, dated 17.02.2018 and the same was handed over to the District Medical and Health Officer, Wanaparthy, at present the Medical and Health Department has already constructed the Hospital Building.

Therefore,
indulgence of this Court is not warranted.
Hence, seeks to dismiss the writ petition.

6. Recording the submissions made by both the learned counsel, this Court without going into the merits and demerits of the case deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition granting liberty to the petitioner - Society and all affected parties to work out the remedies in accordance with law before an appropriate forum.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending, shall stand closed.
E.V.VENUGOPAL, J Dated: 02.09.2025 VSU M/S. Vidya Nagar Plot Owners ... vs The Principal Secretary on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41610970/
